title: Agentic AI: Threats and Mitigations
report_type: community threat taxonomy and mitigation guide
system_and_deployment_scope: Autonomous and agentic AI applications, including multi-agent interactions
interaction_dependency: Provides the parent threat taxonomy later specialized by the OWASP multi-agent threat-modeling guide
threat_model: Goal manipulation; tool misuse; identity abuse; memory poisoning; insecure communication; cascading failures
method: Expert-developed threat model and mitigation taxonomy
finding: Identifies agent autonomy, tools, memory, identity, and interactions as security boundaries requiring layered controls
limitations: Community guidance; does not estimate empirical prevalence or comparative defense effectiveness
conflict_of_interest: OWASP is a nonprofit community project
evidence_locations: Official OWASP release page and downloadable guide

title: Guide for Securing the AI-Powered Enterprise: Getting Started with AI Applications
system_and_deployment_scope: Enterprise AI applications including collaborating agentic systems
interaction_dependency: Identifies collaboration autonomy and real-time decisions as agentic risk multipliers
threat_model: Prompt injection; data leakage; excessive autonomy; compliance failures
method: Enterprise guidance and phased adoption framework
finding: Recommends governance data protection threat controls and oversight for agentic AI
limitations: Broad enterprise scope and limited MAS-specific evidence
conflict_of_interest: Microsoft describes its own products and practices
evidence_locations: Official Microsoft publication page; agentic AI section

title: Multi-Agentic System Threat Modeling Guide v1.0
system_and_deployment_scope: Multi-agent systems with coordinating autonomous agents
interaction_dependency: Applies an agentic threat taxonomy to multi-agent architectures and trust boundaries
threat_model: Compromised agents; inter-agent manipulation; orchestration and shared-state threats
finding: Documents additional attack surfaces introduced by coordination communication shared memory and orchestration
limitations: Community guidance rather than an empirical prevalence study
conflict_of_interest: OWASP is a nonprofit community project
evidence_locations: Official release page; guide title page and architecture/threat sections

title: Google's Approach for Secure AI Agents
system_and_deployment_scope: AI agents controlled by people and connected to tools services and other agents
interaction_dependency: Requires controllers bounded powers and observable planning/actions across interactions
threat_model: Prompt injection; confused deputy; excessive authority; compromised dependencies
finding: Advocates defense in depth combining deterministic controls and reasoning-based defenses
limitations: Aspirational provider framework rather than an independent evaluation
conflict_of_interest: Google describes its own security approach
evidence_locations: Official Google Research page and linked whitepaper

title: Achieving a Secure AI Agent Ecosystem
system_and_deployment_scope: AI agent ecosystems including interactions with APIs humans and other agents
interaction_dependency: Treats agent-to-agent interaction identity delegation and ecosystem dependencies as security boundaries
threat_model: Compromised or untrusted agents; ecosystem and supply-chain adversaries
finding: Calls for identity authorization monitoring and ecosystem-level security mechanisms
limitations: Broad agent ecosystem scope; not a systematic MAS literature review
conflict_of_interest: Funded and published by Schmidt Sciences
evidence_locations: Chapter 1; sections on multiagent systems identity and communication

title: Agentic AI Identity and Access Management: A New Approach
system_and_deployment_scope: Complex multi-agent systems with dynamic identities delegation and cross-protocol interactions
interaction_dependency: Focuses on identity lifecycle delegation revocation and policy propagation across agent interactions
threat_model: Identity spoofing; stale authorization; delegation abuse; cross-domain trust failure
finding: Proposes agent IDs DIDs verifiable credentials contextual access control and a security backplane
limitations: Conceptual architecture without a comparative empirical benchmark
conflict_of_interest: CSA is an industry nonprofit with participating vendors
evidence_locations: Official CSA artifact page; architecture and multi-agent IAM sections

title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
system_and_deployment_scope: Autonomous agent applications and complex agent workflows
interaction_dependency: Includes insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures, rogue agents, identity and privilege abuse, and human-agent trust exploitation
threat_model: Ten prioritized agentic application risk families
method: Globally peer-reviewed practitioner framework developed with more than 100 contributors
metric_and_denominator: Ranked practitioner risk list rather than a benchmark denominator
finding: Offers an operational risk vocabulary for design, testing, and governance of agentic applications
limitations: Prioritization framework, not a complete census of vulnerabilities or attacks
evidence_locations: Official OWASP resource page and Top 10 document

title: Cisco's Integrated AI Security and Safety Framework
system_and_deployment_scope: AI lifecycle including multi-agent orchestration shared memory and MCP
interaction_dependency: Includes multi-agent coordination as a first-class design element and attack surface
threat_model: Multi-agent manipulation; collusion; memory corruption; tool and supply-chain exploitation
finding: Provides techniques and subtechniques spanning AI security safety and multi-agent risks
limitations: Broader than MAS and presented by a security vendor
conflict_of_interest: Cisco authors and publishes the framework
evidence_locations: Official Cisco framework page; design element 3 and taxonomy description

title: OWASP Vendor Evaluation Criteria for AI Red Teaming Providers and Tooling v1.0
system_and_deployment_scope: Chatbots, RAG, tool-calling agents, MCP architectures, and multi-agent workflows
interaction_dependency: Requires red-team coverage beyond jailbreaks, including tools, protocols, multi-agent workflows, and deployment threat models
threat_model: Realistic adversarial testing of model, implementation, tool, protocol, and workflow boundaries
method: Vendor and tooling assessment criteria with green flags and red flags
metric_and_denominator: Qualitative evaluation criteria, not a pooled performance metric
finding: Distinguishes substantive system-level red teaming from superficial jailbreak-only testing
limitations: Procurement guidance; does not independently validate named vendors
evidence_locations: Official OWASP release page and criteria document

title: A Guide to Agentic AI Security
system_and_deployment_scope: Agent fleets hierarchies orchestrators tools and enterprise APIs
interaction_dependency: Distinguishes risks by an agent's place in a hierarchy or multi-agent ecosystem
threat_model: Prompt injection; unauthorized access; overprivileged orchestration; unsafe tool action
finding: Emphasizes securing the action layer and applying controls according to role and hierarchy
limitations: High-level guidance rather than a systematic evidence synthesis
evidence_locations: Official IBM page; action-layer and hierarchy discussion

title: AI Security Solutions Landscape for Agentic AI Q2 2026
system_and_deployment_scope: Full agentic AI lifecycle at the DevOps and SecOps boundary
interaction_dependency: Maps tools and controls to agentic threat-mitigation duties, including runtime and interaction security
threat_model: OWASP agentic threat taxonomy and lifecycle SecOps tasks
method: Quarterly mapping of open-source and commercial solutions by lifecycle stage and risk coverage
metric_and_denominator: Coverage mapping rather than comparative efficacy benchmark
finding: Shows where current products claim coverage across the agentic lifecycle and where solution gaps remain
limitations: Vendor landscape and claimed coverage do not establish defense effectiveness
conflict_of_interest: Community and industry input; vendors may be represented
evidence_locations: Official OWASP landscape page and downloadable report

title: Zero Trust for Agentic AI: Securing the Enterprise from AI Agents
system_and_deployment_scope: Enterprise agents across cloud SaaS on-premises tools MCP servers and peer agents
interaction_dependency: Applies continuous identity access and behavior controls to agent interactions and propagation
threat_model: Prompt injection; tool misuse; memory poisoning; agent-to-agent manipulation
finding: Proposes knowing every agent authorizing every action and adapting to runtime risk
limitations: Vendor whitepaper without independent product-effectiveness evaluation
conflict_of_interest: Cisco describes a Cisco security architecture
evidence_locations: Official Cisco page and linked whitepaper; key risks and controls

title: OWASP GenAI Exploit Round-up Report Q1 2026
system_and_deployment_scope: Reported GenAI and agentic AI incidents from January through April 11, 2026
interaction_dependency: Includes incidents involving orchestration, agent identity, agentic supply chains, excessive authority, tool misuse, and cascading failures
threat_model: Real-world exploitation and operational failures mapped to OWASP LLM and agentic risk classes
method: Curated incident roundup with source references and CVE mappings where available
metric_and_denominator: Selected major incidents; explicitly not exhaustive
finding: Reports a shift from model-output risks toward identities, orchestration layers, supply chains, privilege abuse, and system-level consequences
limitations: Curated incident report; selection and external reporting quality limit prevalence inference
evidence_locations: Official OWASP report; incident details, risk mappings, and CVE references

organization: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation
title: Summary Analysis of Responses to the Request for Information Regarding Security Considerations for AI Agents
system_and_deployment_scope: AI agents deployed in enterprise and public-sector systems, including interacting and interoperable agents
interaction_dependency: Synthesizes stakeholder concerns about identity, delegated authority, orchestration, communication, standards, and ecosystem-level risk
threat_model: Prompt injection; excessive agency; identity and authorization failure; compromised tools; supply-chain and cross-agent risk
method: Government synthesis of public RFI responses
metric_and_denominator: Not applicable; qualitative synthesis of submitted responses
finding: Respondents broadly agreed that existing cybersecurity practices remain relevant but require adaptation for agent security, standards, and information sharing
limitations: Public-comment synthesis rather than an independent exploit benchmark or prevalence study
evidence_locations: Official NIST publication page; NIST Trustworthy and Responsible AI report 800-5

title: AIUC-1: Crosswalks OWASP Top 10 For Agentic Applications
system_and_deployment_scope: Agentic applications governed under AIUC-1 and OWASP controls
interaction_dependency: Maps controls for insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures, rogue agents, identity, privilege, and trust exploitation
threat_model: OWASP agentic Top 10 mapped to AIUC-1 control requirements
method: Bidirectional framework crosswalk and gap analysis
metric_and_denominator: Control coverage and eight identified priority gap areas
finding: Identifies control gaps in agent identity, runtime containment, architectural monitoring, supply-chain attestation, and schema enforcement
limitations: Framework mapping rather than implementation or exploit evaluation
evidence_locations: Official OWASP crosswalk page and downloadable document

title: State of Agentic AI Security and Governance 2.01
system_and_deployment_scope: Autonomous AI systems, enterprise governance, security controls, and regulatory frameworks
interaction_dependency: Covers governance and security of increasingly autonomous and interconnected agents
threat_model: Agentic application risks, weak governance, identity, tool, memory, supply-chain, and runtime-control failures
finding: Maps current governance models, standards, and operational controls for secure agentic deployment
limitations: Broad landscape report and not exclusively multi-agent
evidence_locations: Official OWASP version 2.01 release page and report
